change.summary: Propagate the existing bounded failure-callback signal into retryable upstream-failure circuit and route persistence so an abandoned private checkpoint cannot retain the serialized selector after the total deadline.

before_implementation.observed_failure: The first request received its bounded total-deadline response after one pre-semantic fixture 5xx, but the stalled attempt-failure checkpoint retained the routing lock so the manual next-request route did not settle within 100 milliseconds.
before_implementation.bounded_cleanup: The synthetic state-store gate was settled during fixture cleanup and the command exited normally.

failure_injections: fixture account A returns a classified upstream 5xx before semantic output
the first attempt-failure circuit checkpoint remains pending beyond the 250 millisecond total deadline
the old callback releases the serialized routing lock after deadline abandonment
a fixture manual next-request route to B is accepted while the old save remains pending
a later separate new request uses B and succeeds with new_backend_session status

covers: HTTP/SSE bounded pre-semantic failover and post-semantic no-replay
WebSocket bounded pre-semantic failover and post-semantic no-replay
durable and abortable automatic routing plus durable manual routing
abortable credential, auth-failure, half-open and attempt-failure checkpoints

strict_matrix.first_attempt_reason: The invocation omitted the required umask 0022; four temporary-file permission fixtures failed without a product assertion or production-state change.

qualification_invocation_notes: The first strict-matrix invocation omitted the required umask 0022 and produced four temporary-file permission-fixture failures; the only permitted retry used the correct umask and passed 291/291.

deployment.reason: The previously proven sudo root-GID transition failure and non-writable /opt/codex-account-router boundary are unchanged.

remaining_limits: 0.2.18 is verified but is not active until a host-privileged operator runs the rollback-capable router-only deployment script.
AbortSignal abandonment does not cancel an already-issued atomic state save. Later operations are separate new requests, not continuation of the timed-out request.
A manual next-request route acceptance does not migrate an existing backend session or recover in-flight work.
The timed-out request is not replayed or resumed. Only a later new request can use another eligible account.
The tests use synthetic accounts only and do not qualify a real A-to-B switch.
Real two-account verification remains blocked until explicit enrollment authorization.
